modules.title: Lesson One
modules.summary: This lesson will tackle how art is defined, why it matters, what is it for, and some preliminary assumptions that people normally hold about art.

notes.title: Introduction
notes.content:
This lesson will tackle how art is defined, why it matters, what is it for, and some preliminary assumptions that people normally hold about art. How can we read and understand a work of art? What can we learn from studying art? Thus, you will engage yourselves to answering questions that challenge different views about art. You will be able to recognize your understanding of art, and potentially build a wider, more comprehensive view of the nature and definition of art through visual analysis, one which answers those conceptual challenges.

In this lesson, you will be asked to identify and discuss, and clarify certain views and perceptions about art.

notes.title: Lecture Notes: Defining Art
notes.content:
It most certain that art is all around us. In fact, it is universal as it can be found in all cultures. This is a basic assumption of what art is. Much more, art has been around for thousand of years and through the ages it has evolved in a number of different ways and the reasons for creating it vary from person to person, culture to culture, and from a time period to another on a number of factors.

Besides, just imagine what the world be like without art. How would the things we see around us look? How would nature look? Could anything like beauty, what would be visually appealing exists at all? It is a provocative question that necessitates defining what art is or is not.

notes.title: Lecture Notes: Why Art Matters
notes.content:
The thing about art is that it is so diverse that there are so many ways to understand it as there are people. That is why there are scholars from different fields who give their own definition of the word and whether or not it is the best definition, the point is that people look at art based on how they experience it. So art involves experience- another basic assumption.

But why do we study art? Do you think art is important? Indeed, art has a particular importance in our lives.

Art has a purpose, as well as expression; they occupy some place in our way of looking at life and the world. Art has a unique role in moving people- providing a source of inspiration, inciting new questions and provoking curiosity, and even revolutionary ideas or socio-cultural, and political advocacies- it is an essential ingredient to empowering people (especially among the younger generation.)

For example, when activists show images of extra judicial killings (EJK) in their campaigns, this is the art pulling the heartstrings of the society’s government and its forces to make radical changes.

Thus, art can potentially influence our culture, politics, and even the economy.

From this point of view, art helps develop critical thinking and the ability to interpret the world around us. We might say that art requires thought- some kind of creative impulse. What does this mean? Art is not just limited to absorbing information. Rather, it makes you think about current ideas and inspire you to make your own. And as students, art encourages self-expression and creativity- it unlocks the potentials of the human mind. This is a basic assumption of art- it is a human creation, utilizing our thoughtful skill and artistry.

notes.title: Lecture Notes: What is Art made for?
notes.content:
Whether or not we are aware of it, we allow arts to affect our lives one way or another and the reasons why we make art are many!

But what is art made for? An inquiry on what art is for is an inquiry on the function of art. For example, what do you think is the installed art infront of Holy Angel University (HAU) Theater for?

Within art, there exist purposes referred to as functions for which a piece of art may be designed, but no art can be "assigned" a function—either in scholarly studies or casual conversation—outside of the proper context. Art forms exist within very specific contexts that must be considered when classifying them. Whether a particular piece of art has existed for centuries or has yet to be created, it is functional in some way—all art exists for a reason and these reasons make up the functions of art. When it comes to function, different art forms come with distinctive functions.

The functions of art normally fall into three categories: physical, social, and personal.

### 1. Personal Function
- Functions of art are highly varied and subjective, depending on the artist who creates art.
- Artist can create art out of self-expression, enjoyment, meant to provoke thought, or therapeutic purposes.

### 2. Social Function
- Art is used for public display and celebration.
- It is used to affect collective behavior- addresses a particular collective interest as opposed to one’s personal point of view or experience.

### 3. Physical Function
- This function of art can be realized through the objects and environments we create which fills a utilitarian need.

notes.title: Lecture Notes: How is Art classified?
notes.content:
Traditional and contemporary art encompasses activities as diverse as:

Architecture, sculpture, painting, music, theater, dance, printmaking, opera, photography, literature, filmmaking, furnitures, ceramics to name a few.

All these activities are commonly classified into these generally accepted categories:

### 1. Visual Arts
These are art forms that create works that are primarily visual in nature, such as, drawing, painting, sculpture, photography, printmaking, and architecture.

### 2. Performing/Combined Arts
These are art forms that combine variety of media or materials which can be both seen and heard, and which exists in both space and time. Examples are music, dance, film, theater, and literature.

### 3. Digital Arts
It is work made with digital technology or presented on digital technology. This includes images done completely on computer or any electronic device using multiple social media platforms.

### 4. Applied Art
It is an art form in which artistic design is applied to utilitarian objects or items of everyday use such as furniture design, interior design, fashion design, and graphic design.
